answer: A finished thread needs three stages, each signed by a different identity. Stages are forge smelting, ferrous handling, and thread spinning. One key signs only one stage per output; signing two voids it and burns both bonds. Each stage locks a 60-credit bond and pays a 40-credit fee, so a fake thread costs its operator 300 across three stages, while an honest maker pays only 100 for its stage. The k-th fake identity still pays 100, so 1,000 cost 100,000 for just 333 finished threads. A role-hoarding ring fails on key reuse: the ledger spots the duplicate signature and burns the bonds.
